items.label: L3Harris Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Ken Sharp on radios and electronic warfare: Falcon IV wi

set.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on radios and electronic warfare: Falcon IV will move to Falcon V, 'a whole new radio' about half the size with better battery life and more capacity, rolling out around the end of next year (international customers move from Falcon III to Falcon IV); U.S. radio modernization is at '40-plus percent'. Counter-UAS has a '$1 billion in pipeline' - its first round fires '$30,000 missiles at drones' with a kill rate of 'about 80%' and has been fielded in Ukraine - and L3Harris is working with SOCOM on Wraith Shield-type software jamming. Next Generation Jammer is on schedule and on price, in a cost-type development phase with lower margins. Margin focus: a clean 16% margin without asset-sale gains, fewer EAC charges through management reserve, missile volumes going '3x, 4x, 5x, 10x' on different programs, and the former Remington facility in Huntsville to dual-source parts where suppliers create issues.

items.reason: The Jefferies transcript never names VAMPIRE (that name appears only in the 09-16 Morgan Stanley talk); the CFO said 'Our first round of that is really kind of firing $30,000 missiles at drones'.
items.evidence: Our first round of that is really kind of firing $30,000 missiles at drones. The kill rate on it is about 80%.

items.label: Pfizer Morgan Stanley conference 2026 (09-14-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Albert Bourla: Pfizer's new products and business-develo

set.signal: CEO Albert Bourla: Pfizer's new products and business-development products are running at around a $13 billion annualized rate and growing in the 20s percent, the basis for offsetting the coming LOEs. The HHS 340B pilot starting in January 2027 covers two significant Pfizer products, ELIQUIS and IBRANCE (a pilot Pfizer 'worked very hard to make sure that happens'); he would not count on a major 340B benefit, as the recent effect was net marginally positive.

items.reason: Beating 'expectations' is measured against analyst consensus estimates, which the capture rules exclude; the rest of the entry is unchanged.
items.evidence: In the last 10 earnings ... we beat expectations for revenue, nine out of 10, and for EPS, 10 out of 10.
